sources.entry: pwa2play by degordonstech - Packages a PWA into a signed Play Store Android bundle with Bubblewrap and checks target API level, signing key reuse, assetlinks fingerprints and version codes before upload.

summary.one_liner: A Claude Code plugin that guides packaging a PWA as a Trusted Web Activity Android app and checking the key rules before a Google Play upload.
summary.what_it_does: The plugin wraps Google's Bubblewrap tool to build a Trusted Web Activity, a small Android app that opens a website full screen without browser chrome once the site proves ownership via assetlinks. It provides three slash commands: /pwa2play:package walks through a first release (init, build, assetlinks file, first upload), /pwa2play:update rebuilds an existing app for a new release while keeping the signing key and version code correct, and /pwa2play:check reads the package id, version code, target SDK and min SDK from a built .apk. A skill is also pulled in automatically when the user discusses publishing a PWA to Android. The README lists rules the plugin encodes: reuse one signing key for every update, put the app signing SHA-256 from Play Console into assetlinks.json, raise the version code each upload, target the current API level, and use a test track (personal accounts need a 12-tester, 14-day closed test before production).
use_cases: Publishing a PWA to the Google Play Store
Packaging a website as an Android Trusted Web Activity
Fixing browser address bar showing in a TWA app
Preparing an app update without signing key rejection
Checking an APK's version code and target SDK before upload
Setting up assetlinks.json for Digital Asset Links
how_to_run: Run npm install once inside the plugin folder (needed for the check command)
Use /pwa2play:package for a first release, /pwa2play:update for later releases, /pwa2play:check to inspect a built .apk
stack: Node npm package for the check script
notable: Encodes the common Play Store rejection traps (signing key reuse, assetlinks fingerprint, version codes, target API level) as guided steps
Three slash commands plus an automatically invoked skill
check command reads package id, version code and SDK levels directly from a built APK
Explains the 12-tester, 14-day closed test requirement for personal accounts
caveats: Requires a live PWA served over HTTPS with a valid web manifest and a Google Play developer account
The check command needs an npm install step inside the plugin folder
Target API level requirement changes roughly each August, so the guidance needs ongoing updating
